# FlatHill

> FlatHill is developing a U.S. robotics hardware supply platform based on proprietary joint module designs and manufacturing expertise.

## Products and strategy
- Micro-drive families: M01, M01 Neo and M02. Larger joint families: WZ53, WZ79 and WZ119. Maturity varies by SKU. Large-joint values in source material are design targets.
- Platform families: dexterous hands, quadrupeds, spherical robots and fixed dual-arm systems.
- Phase 1: component supply, paid engineering and documented U.S. manufacturing using qualified global inputs.
- Phase 2, after 2027: intended ROSE software workflows from scratch to demo and from demo to mass production, with staged U.S. production cells. Management reports an early prototype; no verified feature list is available in this presentation.
- Phase 3: controlled recursive improvement of hardware and manufacturing processes, subject to engineering validation and release approval.

## Evidence and assumptions
- All BOM allocations in the investor deck are illustrative design budgets. The 80% domestic component-cost target is not an audited achieved percentage or an equipment authorization.
- U.S.-supplier purchasing spend is different from qualifying domestic component cost.
- The FCC definition of foreign-produced refers to FAR 25.101(a). The general cost test is above 65% through 2028 and above 75% from 2029, with applicable exceptions and a U.S. manufacture requirement.
- No completed FCC clearance, reviewed FTO opinion, current customer contracts or FlatHill shipment totals are established by the deck.
- Team-provided 150+ prior-career robot deliveries are not FlatHill sales.
- The $8–10M financing range is an existing September 2026 working plan, not a closed round. Roadmap dates are planning assumptions.

## Interactive investor story
- Primary volume channel: U.S. robotics OEM programs. Applied-AI labs provide early paid validation. Integrators provide an expansion channel. These are target segments, not confirmed customers.
- Commercial sequence: paid evaluation, design-in, repeat production orders, then ROSE and manufacturing services.
- Market context: A3 reports $2.25B of North American robot orders in 2025. This is not FlatHill TAM.
- Interactive revenue model: hypothetical programs * robots per program/year * modules per robot * module price. Defaults are 5 * 500 * 12 * $180 = $5.4M annual component revenue, with an assumed 30% gross margin. These are neither a forecast nor signed pipeline.
